name: Sonnet+tools price momentum
strategy: Long the strongest data-verified 12-1 momentum sector/name themes (energy, healthcare, biotech, financials), cutting whichever leg's momentum has broken versus the group, with cash sized to macro-shock risk.
reassessment_note: Momentum check across the six legs plus a hard macro re-read ahead of the 9/16 FOMC print. XLE is the clear winner: $65.32, near its 52-week high, +47.68% YTD, and financial-media coverage today reads 'Energy Eyes Breakout as XLV Slips' -- a direct momentum divergence signal in the group's own favor. IWD is the second-strongest: $253.81, +22.35% YTD, +27.42% 1yr, near its 52-week high, outperforming its Large Value category by roughly 3x with no idiosyncratic red flags. Both get sized up. On the other side, GS has clearly broken momentum versus the group -- -6.29% over the past month, -1.46% intraday today, and the leg is already -5.11% since the 9/8 entry, the worst in the book by a wide margin -- so per the strategy's own cutting rule it goes to zero rather than being nursed along into an Oct 13 earnings date. XBI's short-term momentum has also cracked (-1.88% over the month, -2.00% intraday today) even though the 6-month trend is still positive; biotech is a long-duration, financing-sensitive group and is the wrong risk to carry into a hawkish rate event, so it is cut to zero rather than held at a reduced size. XLV shows the same 'slips' pattern in today's tape and the weakest YTD return of the group (+7.68%), so it is trimmed hard (21% to 8%) but kept as a small low-rate-sensitivity ballast rather than cut outright. XLF is weak and falling premarket/afternoon again today, but large-cap diversified-funding banks are a plausible net beneficiary of a rate hike via wider margins (unlike GS specifically), so it is trimmed (14% to 10%) rather than eliminated. On the FOMC itself: my own pull of the investing.com Fed Rate Monitor Tool (updated 9/15 9:25am ET) showed roughly 90% odds on a move away from the current hold level versus ~10% on staying put; taken alone that reading was ambiguous on direction because the tool's own labels for the two outcome bands looked inverted. I cross-checked against a live Yahoo Finance pull on GS, which reported Goldman Sachs's own economists now expect 'a 25-basis-point Fed rate hike this week' on inflation concerns, and against parallel desk research circulating in this same poll citing CME FedWatch at ~90-92% priced for a 25bp hike on 9/16, alongside a Brent/WTI spike toward the high-$90s to $100+ on Middle East supply disruption and a 10-year yield pushing toward multi-year highs. Reconciling the two: I am treating the dominant, corroborated read as hike-not-cut, which is exactly the kind of inflation shock XLE is priced to benefit from and exactly the kind of duration/multiple compression that argues against carrying GS and XBI at meaningful size. Because this is a binary, same-day macro event with real disagreement across desks about which way the ~90% number points, I am also sizing cash up from 12% to 34% as the shock buffer the strategy's mandate calls for, rather than staying fully invested through the print. Net: gross exposure falls from 88% to 66%, two broken-momentum legs (GS, XBI) are cut to zero, the two strongest momentum legs (XLE, IWD) are sized up, and XLF/XLV are trimmed rather than eliminated to keep some diversification. This is a full book replacement, not a hold, because three of six legs needed to change size or exit and cash needed to move materially ahead of the print.

positions.thesis: Strongest momentum leg in the book: trading near its 52-week high at $65.32, +47.68% YTD versus a 33.40% category average, with today's sector coverage explicitly framing it as breaking out while healthcare slips. Directly levered to the oil-driven inflation shock (Middle East supply disruption pushing crude toward/above $100) that is also the reason the Fed is being read hawkish into 9/16 -- energy is the textbook beneficiary of that combination. Sized up from 20% to 28% as the highest-conviction leg.

Second-strongest momentum leg: $253.81, near its 52-week high, +22.35% YTD (about 3x its Large Value category average) and +27.42% over 1yr, with no idiosyncratic negative news found. Large-cap value is the natural rotation destination when a hawkish Fed and rising long yields compress duration-sensitive growth multiples, and IWD's ~1,000-name breadth makes it the lowest single-name risk way to size up into FOMC event risk. Increased from 8% to 20%.

Momentum has stalled -- down again premarket and into the afternoon today, YTD +5.43% trailing its own category -- so this is trimmed, not added to. Kept at reduced size rather than cut because large-cap, diversified-funding financials are a plausible net beneficiary of a rate hike via wider net interest margins, which is a materially different risk than the single-name GS position being cut below. Reduced from 14% to 10%.

Weakest momentum of the surviving legs -- 'Healthcare Stocks Fall Pre-Bell Tuesday' and 'XLV Slips' in today's coverage, and the group's weakest YTD return at +7.68% -- so this is cut hard per the strategy's rule to trim legs whose momentum has broken versus the group. Kept at a small size rather than zero because health care is one of the least rate-sensitive sectors in the book and adds diversification against the FOMC's binary outcome. Reduced from 21% to 8%.
